card.name: Verbs before amounts in news reports
card.fires_on: The word right after a future or conditional helper (will, would, is) in news text, where a quantity such as a cost, a duration or a sum comes next. Typical words are take, spend, cost, add and worth.

modes.label: Verb before a cost or time
modes.description: A verb like take, spend, cost or add after will or would, followed by a number of dollars or months.
modes.example: On Tuesday, Nissin said it will<< spend>> $23.5 million to buy

modes.label: Linking word before a figure
modes.description: A word such as of or worth that leads into a measured amount.

card.writes: It pushes the model away from time words like tomorrow and press, and does not clearly promote any one word.
card.plain: It fires on the verb in a news sentence that is about to state an amount, like how much something will cost or how long it will take.
